questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to France and speak French

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The place was really nice, the Uni not as nice.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was really hard to know where to choose courses and we got our schedule very late, like after three weeks. I think that the system could've been exlplained better.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was some infodays in the beginning, but most of it was school and related to how to have the courses in French. The background on French law and the information days overlapped, which was unfortunate.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was very lucky to get accommodation in Cité Universitaire. Otherwise I would've tried other places where one could live with other people.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: There is really no campus on school, but it is important to get accommodation in good time.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The 5 is for Cité Universitaire and Fondation Danoise

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Registration should happen from a platform, and it took a long time to fill in. I received two forms, one of which I didn't even have to fill out. So that was kind of annoying. Also we first got our student cards a month into uni, which was problematic, because we had to get them to enter. The OLA has also been a burden and hard to get signed.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Not much, it could be translated to a bad English. Otherwise there was help when choosing the courses definitively.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful, some of the courses overlapped, but I got to choose from all three years of the licenses and first year of master.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Know what courses you would like to get and talk to other students about what the exam might be.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was hard to study for the exam as they were very different from the ones in Copenhagen and there was little to no reading.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: In my opinion the level was good. In philosophie du droit it was kind of anticipated that you had some more background knowledge.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It is very different. They don't have books and the preparation for the exam is looking up your own notes.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Philosophie du droit (sans TD), Droit de l'Union européenne (avec TD), Introduction au droit historique (sans TD). French law of obligations, French constitutionnel law.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Droit de l'Union Europenne was great, because I had some background knowledge, I think the English courses were good as well.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had to get a French phone number in order to not pay way to much on my danish phone bill, but after I had done that, there was no problem.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I thought I would have to buy books. Food is expensive en Paris, but it is kind of similar to Copenhagen.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't go and I don't know anyone who went. I did sports at Cité U instead.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was different kind of sports opportunities, I didn't sign up for any.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I think the sports could've been fun, I just had better opportunities where I stayed.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I went partying a lot with the people I stayed with. I think that taking time out to see Paris is very good, also I went to Giverny which was amazing.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, it takes a few days to adjust and move in, but I feel like when the school started it was very easy to fit in.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Hmm the school doesn't help with that, the best way is to ask them if they can help with anything, or to try to be as openminded as possible. I feel like it is easier to connect with other Erasmus students than Parisians.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The language barrier, and it would be nice if the school did something to connect the foreign students and the local ones. It is okay that they didn't I did meet a few, and I also had my main social circle in the Cité Universitaire, so I didn't really search for new ones.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I did appreciate the fact that whenever I was in stores and spoke French they would slow down and answer in French.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1. Get to know what the exams are before signing up for a course. 2. Choose a course which juridical content you have some idea of in danish/know, then it'll get easier if it is in French. 3. Start the semester by asking one of the peers for help, that'll make the semester a lot easier.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I think that it is very important to state that it is a law school and it is one of the top law schools (if not the one) in France, and you have to keep that in mind when being an Erasmus there. Also have patience with the administration office - they are VERY slow, however they will fix things.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I got to meet so many new people and I grew so much as a person. I think that having a break from the "commercial" part of law school in UCPH is very good, and getting some other types of challenges.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Having courses in French, going to an oral exam in French and just learning the contents of the courses. In the beginning it was very hard just to be away from home, then I took one weekend in Copenhagen and after I returned everything was much easier.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I can so recommend going on Erasmus

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
